overview:
Ouarzazate is the natural starting point for the Sahara: from here, the road of a thousand kasbahs runs east between the High Atlas and the Jebel Saghro, past oases, gorges and earthen villages, all the way to the dunes of Merzouga. Most desert tours start in Marrakech and spend their first day crossing the Atlas; starting in Ouarzazate, you skip that drive and have time to actually stop and walk.

This private two-day tour follows the road at an easy pace. On the first day you visit the palm grove of Skoura and its 17th-century Kasbah Amridil, pass through the Valley of Roses at Kelaat M'Gouna and climb into the Dades Gorge to see the rock formations and the famous hairpin road before a night in a hotel above the river. On the second day you walk in the Todra Gorge between walls up to 300 m high, cross the desert plains past the khettara water channels and the fossil workshops of Erfoud, and ride a camel into the Erg Chebbi for sunset and a night in a desert camp. You wake up in the dunes for sunrise, and the tour ends in Merzouga after breakfast, ready for your next step.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: 2 days of travel, with nights in the Dades Gorge and in a desert camp
• Start: Ouarzazate (hotel, riad, bus station or airport) – Finish: Merzouga, the morning after the desert night
• Distance: about 370 km, split into two shorter driving days (about 3 and 5 hours of driving)
• Type: private tour with driver
• Activity level: easy; short walks and a 1-hour camel ride
• Meals: dinner and breakfast on both nights

THE ROUTE
Day 1 – Ouarzazate, Skoura palm grove and Kasbah Amridil, Valley of Roses, Dades Gorge.
Day 2 – Todra Gorge, Tinejdad, Erfoud fossils, camel ride into the Erg Chebbi and a desert camp.
Morning of Day 3 – Sunrise over the dunes, breakfast and drop-off in Merzouga.

WHY THIS TOUR WORKS
If you arrive in Ouarzazate by bus, flight or after a Marrakech day trip, this is the easiest way to reach the desert with the best stops on the way – and with far less driving than tours from Marrakech. Splitting the road over two days gives you time at Skoura, in the Dades and in the Todra instead of photo stops through the window.

WHO WILL ENJOY IT
Independent travellers, couples and families heading to the Sahara, travellers continuing from Merzouga to Fes, and anyone who has already seen Marrakech and the Atlas.

WHO MIGHT PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
For a longer loop back to Ouarzazate, see the [4-day Ouarzazate to Merzouga Sahara loop](/en-US/morocco/ouarzazate/tours/4-day-ouarzazate-to-merzouga-desert-tour-a-sahara-loop-via-dades-and-zagora/7c218caf46b760fcc098931b). To discover Ouarzazate itself first, book the [Ouarzazate day tour](/en-US/morocco/ouarzazate/tours/ouarzazate-day-tour-kasbah-taourirt-atlas-film-studios-ait-ben-haddou-skoura-oasis/3ef3b0ce0392e15b60d63b2c).

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
Pack a small bag for the desert night – your main luggage stays in the vehicle. Bring warm layers for the evenings (the Dades and the desert are cold at night from November to March), a scarf and sunglasses for the dunes, and cash in dirhams for lunches, entrance fees and tips. From Merzouga you can continue by bus, private transfer or a longer tour to Fes or Marrakech; ask us to arrange it.
descriptions:
What to expect: a short, scenic day along the road of the kasbahs – an oasis, the valley of roses and the red cliffs of the Dades Gorge – with time to walk at each stop.

Your driver picks you up in Ouarzazate in the morning. Forty minutes east you reach Skoura, a large oasis of palms, olive and fruit trees watered by ancient channels and scattered with earthen kasbahs. You visit the 17th-century Kasbah Amridil, still owned by the same family, with its small museum of daily life – olive press, bread oven, old tools – and a roof terrace over the palms. Further on, Kelaat M'Gouna is the town of roses: Damask roses grow in hedges between the fields and are distilled into rose water, and every May the town holds its rose festival. A cooperative shows you how it is made; genuine rose water is cheap here.

After lunch in Boumalne Dades, the road climbs into the Dades Gorge. You pass the rounded rock formations known as the monkey fingers and the red cliffs of Tamellalt, then reach the famous hairpin road that zigzags up the cliff – best seen from the café at the top. Your hotel sits above the river, with dinner and a quiet night.

SCHEDULE (times are estimates)
09:00 – Pick-up in Ouarzazate.
09:45 – Skoura palm grove and Kasbah Amridil (about 1 hour).
11:15 – Kelaat M'Gouna and the Valley of Roses (about 45 min).
12:30 – Lunch in Boumalne Dades (not included).
14:00 – Drive up the Dades Gorge.
15:00 – Rock formations ("monkey fingers") and the hairpin road viewpoint (about 1 hour).
16:30 – Hotel in the Dades Gorge; dinner.

GOOD TO KNOW
• About 160 km and 3 hours of driving – an easy day.
• Kasbah Amridil charges a small entrance fee.
• Nights in the gorge are cool even in spring and autumn.

INCLUDED: private vehicle and driver, hotel night with dinner and breakfast.
NOT INCLUDED: lunch, entrance fees, tips.

WHAT YOU'LL TASTE
Rose water and rose products in Kelaat M'Gouna; a Berber tagine dinner at the hotel; dates from Skoura.

PHOTO SPOTS
• The hairpin road of the Dades Gorge from the café at the top.
• Kasbah Amridil framed by palm trees.
• The red cliffs of the Dades at sunset.

Overnight: hotel in the Dades Gorge.
Meals: dinner.

What to expect: the narrow walls of the Todra Gorge, the desert plains and fossils of the Tafilalet, and a camel ride at sunset into the dunes for a night in a desert camp.

After breakfast you drive east to Tinghir, a long palm oasis below the mountains, and on into the Todra Gorge, where limestone walls up to 300 m high close in to about 10 m apart above a clear stream. You walk through the narrowest section, where climbers often hang on the rock faces. The road then crosses the open desert plains past Tinejdad and its khettara, old underground water channels you can see along the road, to Erfoud, where a workshop shows how the black limestone full of 350-million-year-old fossils is cut and polished.

In the late afternoon the orange dunes of the Erg Chebbi rise on the horizon, some up to about 150 m high. At Merzouga you leave your main luggage in the vehicle and ride a camel into the sand as the dunes turn gold and red. At the camp, dinner is served in a tent, followed by drums around the fire and a sky full of stars. Wake early to climb a dune for sunrise, then return to Merzouga for breakfast; the tour ends there.

SCHEDULE (times are estimates)
08:30 – Depart the Dades Gorge.
09:45 – Walk in the Todra Gorge (about 1 hour).
12:30 – Lunch in Tinghir or Tinejdad (not included).
14:30 – Fossil workshop in Erfoud (about 30 min, optional).
16:30 – Merzouga: camel ride into the dunes (about 1 hour).
18:30 – Desert camp: sunset, dinner, music and stars.
Next morning – Sunrise over the dunes, breakfast, drop-off in Merzouga.

GOOD TO KNOW
• About 210 km and 5 hours of driving with stops.
• Bring a small bag for the camp; the camp has blankets and toilets.
• Buying fossils is entirely optional.
• If you do not want to ride, you can walk or reach the camp by 4x4.

INCLUDED: private vehicle and driver, camel ride, camp night with dinner and breakfast, drop-off in Merzouga.
NOT INCLUDED: lunch, drinks, tips.

PHOTO SPOTS
• The narrowest part of the Todra in morning light.
• Camel shadows on the dunes at sunset.
• Sunrise from the top of a dune.

Overnight: desert camp in the Erg Chebbi.
Meals: breakfast, dinner.

WHAT YOU TAKE AWAY: the oases, gorges and dunes of the south in two relaxed days, and the arrival in the Sahara at the best hour.

faq.question: Where does the tour end?
faq.answer: In Merzouga, after the night in the desert camp, sunrise over the dunes and breakfast – usually around 08:30 on the third morning.

faq.question: Is the desert night included?
faq.answer: Yes. The camel ride, the night in a camp among the Erg Chebbi dunes, dinner and breakfast are all included.

faq.question: Is it private?
faq.answer: Yes. The vehicle and driver are only for your group, so you can stay longer at a stop, skip one or change the timing.

faq.question: Can I continue to Fes or Marrakech?
faq.answer: Yes. We can arrange a private transfer from Merzouga to Fes (about 7–8 hours) or Marrakech (about 9–10 hours), or a longer tour. The daily Supratours bus is a cheaper option.

faq.question: Which meals are included?
faq.answer: Dinner and breakfast each night (Dades hotel and desert camp). Lunches are not included so you can choose where to eat.

faq.question: How much driving is there?
faq.answer: About 3 hours on Day 1 and 5 hours on Day 2, including stops. Starting in Ouarzazate saves you the 4-hour crossing of the High Atlas from Marrakech.

faq.question: Can you pick us up at Ouarzazate airport or bus station?
faq.answer: Yes. We pick up at your hotel or riad, Ouarzazate airport or the bus station. Tell us your arrival time and we adjust the start.

faq.question: What is the desert camp like?
faq.answer: A camp of Berber-style tents in the dunes with beds, blankets and toilets. Standard camps have shared bathrooms; luxury camps have private tents with en-suite showers, depending on the package.

faq.question: Can I do the camel ride with no experience?
faq.answer: Yes. The camels walk slowly and each is led by a cameleer. The ride takes about an hour. You can also walk or go by 4x4 if you prefer.

faq.question: Is it suitable for children?
faq.answer: Yes. The drives are short, and children love the camels, the dunes and the gorge streams. Child seats are available on request.

faq.question: When is the best time to go?
faq.answer: March to May and September to November are ideal. Summer days are very hot in the desert; winter nights are cold but the days are clear and sunny.

faq.question: What should I pack?
faq.answer: A small overnight bag for the camp, warm layers for the evenings, a scarf and sunglasses for the dunes, comfortable shoes and sunscreen.

faq.question: Can we add a second night in the desert?
faq.answer: Yes. A second night in Merzouga lets you add a 4x4 tour around the dunes, the Gnawa village of Khamlia and a slower morning. Ask us for the price.
